$schema-note: Consumed by tools/ci/arb_translate.py `extract`. `doNotTranslate` lists proper nouns/brands/acronyms that must be copied verbatim into every locale. `terms` maps dance-domain jargon to a short note pinning the *intended* meaning, so an assisted translation (or a human) renders the dance sense rather than an everyday homograph (e.g. `caller` is the person who prompts the dance, not a telephone caller). This is guidance, not a hard gate; keep it small and high-signal. `register` gives, per locale, how the UI addresses the user; `extract` includes the batch locale's line so a translation keeps one voice.

register.de: Informal: du / dich / dir / dein, and du-imperatives ('Wähle', 'Gib … ein', 'Versuche es erneut'). Never Sie / Ihnen / Ihr. Maintainer decision, 2026-11-27.
register.nl: Informal: je / jouw, never u / uw (the majority voice when the pre-release audit found three 'u' strings, 2026-11).

caller.note: The person who teaches and prompts a social dance in real time. NOT a telephone caller. Many languages keep the English 'caller' as a loanword in the folk-dance community — prefer the established local term only if one genuinely exists.

call.note: The spoken prompt a caller gives dancers (verb: to call a dance). Dance-instruction sense, not a phone call or opening something. de: callen (du callst, gecallt), not aufrufen or ansagen; nl: callen (je callt, gecalld), not bellen.

set.note: The formation of dancers on the floor (e.g. a longways set), or the act of 'setting' as a step. NOT a collection, a settings screen, or 'to set a value'.

figure.note: A named dance movement/pattern (e.g. swing, allemande, hey). NOT a number, illustration, or 'to figure out'.

formation.note: How dancers are arranged before dancing (duple improper, Becket, Sicilian circle, longways, etc.). A structural dance term.

progression.note: How couples move to a new position each time through the dance so they meet new neighbors. A contra/longways structural term, not general 'progress'.

proper.note: A formation state where dancers are on their standard side (opposite of 'improper'). Dance-technical term, not 'correct/appropriate'.

improper.note: A common contra formation where certain dancers have crossed to the opposite side. Dance-technical term — NOT 'inappropriate'.

indecent.note: A specific duple formation name (a variant of proper/improper). Dance jargon — do NOT render as 'obscene'.

hey.note: A weaving figure where dancers pass in a set pattern (a 'hey for four'). A dance figure, not the interjection 'hey'.

allemande.note: A turn where dancers grasp arms/hands and rotate. Keep as 'allemande' unless a well-established local dance term exists.

balance.note: A dance figure: step and balance toward/away from a partner. The step sense, not financial/equilibrium 'balance'.

beat.note: One count of the music, the unit a figure's length is counted in (an 8-beat swing). Not a bar: a bar is a group of beats (see 'bar'). de: Schlag/Schläge (not Takt/Takte, which means bar); nl: tel/tellen (not 'beats').

beats.note: One count of the music, the unit a figure's length is counted in (an 8-beat swing). Not a bar: a bar is a group of beats (see 'bar'). de: Schlag/Schläge (not Takt/Takte, which means bar); nl: tel/tellen (not 'beats').

swing.note: A buoyant rotating figure danced with a partner. The dance figure, not a playground swing or musical swing.

promenade.note: A figure where a couple travels together in a hold. Dance sense.

neighbor.note: The dancer(s) you dance with besides your partner, changing as the dance progresses. Dance-role term.

partner.note: Your primary dance partner for the whole dance. Dance-role term.

square.note: A dance form / formation for four couples in a square. When it labels the dance form, it is a proper form name.

contra.note: A folk dance form danced in long lines of couples. Keep as 'contra'.

mixer.note: A dance in which you change partners over the course of the dance. Dance sense, not a kitchen mixer or audio mixer.

program.note: In this app: a caller's curated, ordered list of dances for an event/evening. NOT a computer program/application. This is a core app noun.

collection.note: In this app: the user's personal library of saved dances. App noun.

dialect.note: In this app: the configurable mapping from canonical move names to the words a particular caller/community uses. App feature name — see the dialect system.

shorthand.note: In this app: a caller's abbreviated notation for a figure. App noun.

duple.note: A minor set of two couples (duple minor). Dance structural term.

triple.note: A minor set of three couples (triple minor). Dance structural term.

longways.note: A formation of couples in two long facing lines. Dance formation name.

note.note: Context-sensitive. For a caller's note (free text on a program slot, figure or dance) use the everyday word for a written note: nl 'notitie', de 'Notiz'; NOT the musical note (nl 'noot', de 'Note'). In diagnostics or import-warning text a 'note' is a short message or remark; translate it as that, not as a musical note.

hook.note: A dance's one-line hook: why you would call this dance. NOT a coat hook or fishing hook; keep the English loanword where no established local term exists (nl 'Hook', not 'Haak').

modifier.note: A group in the dance editor made of a core figure plus ordered modifying figures. Dance-technical term, not a generic 'modifier'; localise it rather than leaving it in English.

perform.note: Perform mode: the large-print live view a caller uses while calling a dance or program. NOT 'performance' as speed/efficiency (de 'Leistung'); the Settings header 'Performance' means Perform-mode display preferences.

performance.note: In the Settings header 'Performance' means Perform-mode display preferences (see 'perform'), NOT speed or efficiency (de 'Leistung').

bar.note: A bar (measure) of music: English country dances are timed in bars, contras in beats. de: Takt/Takte; nl: maat/maten; fr: mesure; da: takt/takter; ja: 小節.

slot.note: One place in a program's set list: a dance, a note or a break. da: slot; de: Slot; fr: créneau; nl: slot; ja: スロット (not plads, Eintrag/Platz, emplacement, plek or 枠). A slot rule is a slot rule in the same word. In a move-wording template, 'slot' instead means a placeholder (see 'placeholder').

placeholder.note: A named gap in a move-wording template, filled from the figure ({hand}). de: Platzhalter; nl: plaatshouder; da: pladsholder.

template.note: A program template: the starting list of dances, notes and breaks a new program can begin from. de: Vorlage; nl: sjabloon; fr: modèle; da: skabelon; ja: テンプレート.

phrase.note: A section of the tune (A1, A2, B1, B2), the unit a dance's figures are grouped by. Dance-music sense.

break.note: A break in a program: a pause between dances. de: Pause; nl: pauze; fr: pause; da: pause; ja: ブレイク. The stored word is always the English token "Break": where a string quotes that token, keep it in English.

event rule.note: A rule a caller sets on a program (no two Becket dances in a row; at most one waltz before the first break). Program-planning sense.

tag.note: A short label the user attaches to a dance. fr: tag (étiquette means a label, a different thing).
